   commands:
   - bash /vllm-workspace/.buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh
   - pytest -v -s distributed/test_elastic_ep.py
+  mirror:
+    amd:
+      label: ':amd: (MI355) Elastic EP Scaling'
+      dind: false
+      device: mi355_4
+      timeout_in_minutes: 180
+      working_dir: /vllm-workspace/tests
+      depends_on:
+      - image-build-amd
+      source_file_dependencies:
+      - vllm/distributed/
+      - vllm/engine/
+      - vllm/v1/executor/
+      - vllm/compilation/
+      - tests/distributed/
+      - vllm/platforms/rocm.py
+      - requirements/kv_connectors_rocm.txt
+      commands:
+      - uv pip install --system -r /vllm-workspace/requirements/kv_connectors_rocm.txt
+      # Early retirement of the replaced groups is real code now, and it removed
+      # the hsa_status 4097 refusal from the scale up: the expert reshuffle on
+      # the fresh groups completes, and in build 95355 a whole scale up with
+      # CUDA graphs and traffic came back with better accuracy than it started.
+      # It did not remove the refusal at the scale down, where the groups being
+      # replaced are still in use and cannot be retired in advance.
+      #
+      # The complete log of build 95867, read from download.txt rather than the
+      # 2 MB the log endpoint returns, separates this group's failures into two
+      # that have nothing in common but the assert they end at. The traceback
+      # line says which is which: line 266 of the test is the scale up, line 273
+      # is the scale back down. Three of the four cases fail on the way up and
+      # the fourth on the way down, in both full passes, and the group pressure
+      # line agrees independently, since only the cases that fail on the way
+      # down ever reach "standby groups for dp=2".
+      #
+      # Going up, the groups are built and the transfer is what dies. Two ranks
+      # report "Memory access fault by GPU node-2" with "Write access to a
+      # read-only page" and "GPU node-3" with "Page not present", always those
+      # two nodes, which are the GPUs of the ranks that just joined, while every
+      # other rank sits in _wait_for_all_transfers. The reason split matters:
+      # a peer's memory imported for reading is mapped read only on the
+      # importing device, and a write to it gives exactly that first reason.
+      #
+      # Coming down, nothing has moved yet. The whole traceback is inside group
+      # creation, create_standby_groups through _init_stateless_group and
+      # PyNcclCommunicator into ncclCommInitRank, which returns "unhandled cuda
+      # error" after rocmemory.cpp reports "Failed to create memory for IPC,
+      # failed with hsa_status: 4097". That is the same stack as the scale down
+      # refusal from build 95233, so it is the known one, not a new one. It is
+      # also not stale communicators: the pressure line immediately before each
+      # of those four failures reads "0 pynccl comm(s)", so early retirement did
+      # its job and the refusal has another cause. No step named scale_down ever
+      # runs, because this kills the path while it is still preparing.
+      #
+      # The slowness on the way up is a consequence of the fault rather than a
+      # second problem. The reshuffle is either under 10 s or over 200 s with
+      # nothing at all in between, and the slow ones follow the fault groups one
+      # for one. The upper band is not a recovery budget, which is how it was
+      # read for several builds: the periodic report has the transfers still at
+      # 16 of 18 in PROC ten seconds before the end, and the duration is printed
+      # in the same second as the SIGTERM the test sends when its own 300 s
+      # deadline expires. So the band is that deadline minus the preparation
+      # ahead of the reshuffle, and nothing recovers.
+      #
+      # Every stall is on layer 0 and on no other layer, 286 reports out of 286,
+      # and no rank ever logs a read for layer 1. That is the first batch of
+      # transfers a freshly built communicator issues, which is where a fresh
+      # RCCL communicator also needed a deferred warm up here, so
+      # VLLM_EEP_WARM_NIXL_TRANSFERS=1 reads one expert's worth from each peer
+      # into scratch and waits for it before the resharding starts. A failure
+      # there is logged and swallowed: it exists to make the real transfers
+      # work, so it must not become the thing that breaks them.
+      #
+      # So one question is left on the way up: does the faulting address fall
+      # inside what the peer registered, or outside it. Inside means a mapping
+      # was revoked under a descriptor that was still correct, and the ticket
+      # belongs to ROCm. Outside means send_base plus src_row times send_stride
+      # walked off the registration, which is arithmetic this repository owns.
+      # Comparing the address against the span a layer reads does not answer it,
+      # because a span sits inside its registration with slack measured at up to
+      # 319 MB, so an address tens of MB outside every span can still be inside
+      # a registration. VLLM_EEP_DEBUG_XFER_DESCS=1 therefore prints the
+      # registered bound next to the span, and the row bound is now checked
+      # before the READ is issued, so our own arithmetic reports itself by name
+      # instead of as an address. VLLM_EPLB_NIXL_XFER_REPORT_S=10 names who is
+      # still in PROC while the wait runs, which separates one stalled layer
+      # from every layer crawling.
+      #
+      # Nothing above says anything about the way down, which fails inside NCCL
+      # rather than inside this repository, and the error it raises asks for the
+      # missing information in so many words: run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO. Both
+      # passes carry it, narrowed to INIT and ALLOC, because ALLOC is what
+      # prints "Allocated shareable buffer" with a size and an ipcDesc, which is
+      # the count of IPC registrations this investigation has wanted since the
+      # first refusal and that ROCm offers no way to read.
+      #
+      # That count now has something to say. At each of the three refusals the
+      # rank held 5.4 to 5.7 GiB of NCCL buffers, and the two on the same device
+      # stopped 6,291,456 bytes apart, which is exactly one buffer, so this
+      # looks like a ceiling rather than a race. Whether anything is released
+      # between reconfigurations is the open half of it: destroy() runs
+      # ncclCommAbort on a daemon thread with join(timeout=5.0) and can return
+      # having freed nothing, which it now says out loud. The summary after each
+      # pass therefore counts ncclCudaFree, Destroy COMPLETE and commAbort next
+      # to the shareable buffers, so the question is answered by a number.
+      #
+      # It goes to NCCL_DEBUG_FILE rather than to the step log, because on
+      # stdout it is unusable: measured locally it adds 2 MB a minute, about
+      # 73 MB per pass, and 62 per cent of that is one tuning line about PXN
+      # repeated. Writing per process keeps stdout clean, verified at zero NCCL
+      # lines on stdout, and the command after each pass prints the tail of each
+      # file with its buffer and init counts, which is where a rank that died
+      # leaves its last state.
+      #
+      # Levers that are dead, each by measurement. UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=n and
+      # UCX_RNDV_SCHEME=get_zcopy both reproduced the fault unchanged in build
+      # 95849, so the rendezvous protocol is not the cause. The glibc malloc
+      # checker ran only in the first pass of that build and the two passes
+      # without it fail identically, so host heap corruption is not the cause
+      # either, which also retires the three unrelated crash sites from earlier
+      # builds. UCX_PROTO_ENABLE=n made a case slow enough that a rank timed out
+      # on the coordination store, and UCX_TLS narrowed to self,tcp left NIXL
+      # unable to register its buffers, so both were discarded locally before
+      # costing CI time.
+      #
+      # The second pass turns off the caching allocator so a freed buffer is
+      # really unmapped instead of handed back from the pool, and that pass is
+      # no longer only a probe. In build 95867 all three cases it reached
+      # climbed from two ranks to four, which only one case in eight managed
+      # while the allocator was on, and then all three died on the way back
+      # down. So the failure going up depends on the allocator and the one
+      # coming down does not, which is the cleanest separation between them so
+      # far. The likely reason is time rather than memory: hipMalloc and hipFree
+      # synchronize the device, so without a pool every allocation becomes a
+      # fence and the overlap a race would need is gone, which is a heavy
+      # version of the targeted synchronize added upstream for the same race.
+      # That makes this pass a test of the race, not a fix for it.
+      #
+      # The file used to run the same command twice before this pass, to see
+      # whether a case that passes keeps passing. It does not need to any more:
+      # in build 95867 the two identical passes failed on exactly the same four
+      # cases, three on the scale up and one on the scale down, so the
+      # repetition has already answered its question. Dropping it halves the
+      # runtime of the step, which matters because the first attempt at that
+      # build was cut off at 1 h 30 min when the agent was stopped, before the
+      # third pass could finish.
+      #
+      # The watchdog stays on at 60 s. Both unbounded waits this investigation
+      # found, drain_async and _wait_for_all_transfers, announced themselves
+      # only as silence, once for two hours with no output at all.
+      #
+      # RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0 is not cosmetic. The four ranks print identical frames
+      # and Ray collapses them into "repeated 4x across cluster", which in
+      # build 95373 cost us every frame of three watchdog dumps.
+      #
+      # Three recurring messages are noise and counting them says so. "Cannot
+      # get amd_mem_obj" appears 6571 times and "Cijk_..." 704 times in a log
+      # whose cases mostly passed, and "UpdateStreams failed" from
+      # hip_graph_internal shows up in all 15 green local iterations, hundreds
+      # of times per run.
+      #
+      # None of this reproduces locally. Fifteen iterations of the whole file
+      # came back green under the same CPU quota, and dropping cma so that the
+      # rendezvous has to run over tcp with rocm_copy, the combination the
+      # crashing stack shows, still passed.
+      #
+      # Two additions answer the one question above, which an address alone
+      # cannot. VLLM_EEP_DEBUG_ALLOC_EXTENTS=1 prints the allocation each
+      # published tensor really falls inside, because an IPC export covers the
+      # whole allocation and not the tensor handed to it, so a tensor cut out of
+      # a pool segment is exported together with every unrelated tensor sharing
+      # that segment, which the owner keeps writing to while a peer holds it
+      # mapped. Locally every one of 432 exports is exactly its tensor, offset
+      # zero and nothing on either side, and these tensors are 176 and 352 MiB
+      # so the allocator gives each its own segment. If that also holds in CI,
+      # the width of the export is retired as a cause. VLLM_EEP_DEBUG_MAPPINGS=1
+      # lists the device backed ranges of the process before any transfer and
+      # then every range that appears later, so a fault address can finally be
+      # placed. The rank that dies is importing as well as being read from, and
+      # a mapping UCX makes when it opens a peer's memory is invisible from
+      # Python but listed by the kernel, so this is the only way to tell a peer
+      # mapping apart from this rank's own memory. It runs on the first and
+      # third pass, where the fault actually happens, and the extents only on
+      # the first, since they do not change between passes.
+      #
+      # The third pass keeps the caching allocator and turns off the UCX
+      # registration cache instead. With a pool a freed buffer comes back at the
+      # same address, so the cache can keep a registration for a range the
+      # allocator has already handed to a different tensor: the owner writes to
+      # that tensor and faults on a write at an address inside no current
+      # registration, which is exactly the shape of the fault. Without a pool an
+      # address is never reused and there is nothing stale to hit, which is why
+      # the second pass passes going up. So this pass asks whether it is the
+      # reuse of addresses rather than the pool itself. UCX_MEM_EVENTS=no is
+      # not the same lever and has already failed: it removes the hooks that
+      # invalidate the cache, so it makes a stale entry more likely, not less.

+    environment, so HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES still maps the index to the same card.
+    """
+    try:
+        out = subprocess.run(
+            [
+                sys.executable,
+                "-c",
+                _CHILD_EXPORT,
+                str(size),
+                str(_hip_device()),
+                str(_MALLOC_FLAGS["uncached"]),
+                str(limit),
+            ],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=120,
+        )
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        return "child timed out"
+    said = out.stdout.strip() or "no output"
+    if out.returncode != 0:
+        return f"child exited {out.returncode}: {said} {out.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"
+    return said

+def _ipc_export_mode() -> str:
+    """Which of ROCr's two export implementations is actually running.
+
+    Runtime::IPCCreate branches on ipc_dmabuf_supported_, which is simply
+    !HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY. One side goes through hsaKmtShareMemory, the
+    other through hsaKmtExportDMABufHandle, so these are different kernel
+    calls, not two spellings of one. The vLLM ROCm images pin the legacy side:
+
+        docker/Dockerfile.rocm:862  ENV HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=1
+
+    Reading the variable back would only tell us what the image set. Decoding
+    the handle tells us which branch ran, because the dmabuf side writes the
+    pointer into words 0 and 1 and the exporting pid into word 2, while the
+    legacy side writes the thunk's own handle there.
+    """
+    hip = _lib()
+    env = os.environ.get("HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY", "unset")
+    ptr = ctypes.c_void_p()
+    rc = hip.hipExtMallocWithFlags(
+        ctypes.byref(ptr), ctypes.c_size_t(6 << 20), ctypes.c_uint(0x3)
+    )
+    if rc != 0:
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        return f"env={env} malloc failed {_err(rc)}"
+    handle = (ctypes.c_ubyte * _HANDLE_BYTES)()
+    rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(handle, ptr)
+    if rc != 0:
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        hip.hipFree(ptr)
+        return f"env={env} export failed {_err(rc)}"
+    words = struct.unpack("<16I", bytes(handle))
+    # ctypes types value as int | None, and the allocation succeeded above, so
+    # read it once into an int rather than guarding it twice below.
+    addr = ptr.value or 0
+    hip.hipFree(ptr)
+    hip.hipGetLastError()
+    dmabuf = (
+        words[0] == (addr & 0xFFFFFFFF)
+        and words[1] == (addr >> 32)
+        and words[2] == os.getpid()
+    )
+    return f"env={env} effective={'dmabuf' if dmabuf else 'legacy'}"
+

+def _ipc_probe(size: int) -> dict[str, str]:
+    hip = _lib()
+    results = {}
+    for name, flags in _MALLOC_FLAGS.items():
+        ptr = ctypes.c_void_p()
+        rc = hip.hipExtMallocWithFlags(
+            ctypes.byref(ptr), ctypes.c_size_t(size), ctypes.c_uint(flags)
+        )
+        if rc != 0:
+            results[name] = f"malloc failed {_err(rc)}"
+            hip.hipGetLastError()
+            continue
+        handle = ctypes.create_string_buffer(64)
+        rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(handle, ptr)
+        if rc == 0:
+            results[name] = "ok"
+        else:
+            results[name] = f"ipc failed {_err(rc)} [{_pointer_facts(ptr)}]"
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        hip.hipFree(ptr)
+    try:
+        tensor = torch.empty(size, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        tensor.untyped_storage()._share_cuda_()
+        results["torch_allocator"] = "ok"
+    except Exception as e:
+        results["torch_allocator"] = f"failed {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
+    return results
+

+    """RCCL exports handles for plain hipMalloc buffers, which the
+    hipExtMallocWithFlags probe above never exercises."""

+    rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(handle, ptr)

+    hip.hipGetLastError()

+def _ipc_probe_burst(size: int, count: int) -> str:
+    """Exports many handles at once without freeing, to see whether the export
+    path has a per-process limit. Everything is released before returning."""
+    hip = _lib()
+    ptrs: list[ctypes.c_void_p] = []
+    outcome = f"all {count} ok"
+    try:
+        for i in range(count):
+            ptr = ctypes.c_void_p()
+            rc = hip.hipMalloc(ctypes.byref(ptr), ctypes.c_size_t(size))
+            if rc != 0:
+                hip.hipGetLastError()
+                outcome = f"malloc failed at {i}: {_err(rc)}"
+                break
+            ptrs.append(ptr)
+            handle = ctypes.create_string_buffer(64)
+            rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(handle, ptr)
+            if rc != 0:
+                hip.hipGetLastError()
+                outcome = f"ipc failed at {i}: {_err(rc)}"
+                break
+    finally:
+        for ptr in ptrs:
+            hip.hipFree(ptr)
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+    return outcome

+def _ipc_export_ceiling(size: int, limit: int) -> str:
+    """How many exports fit before the driver refuses one.
+
+    The flags matter and the earlier version of this probe had them wrong. It
+    went through plain hipMalloc, while RCCL allocates the buffers it exports
+    with hipExtMallocWithFlags and hipDeviceMallocUncached:
+
+        p2p_tmp.cc:284 Cuda Alloc Size 6291456 pointer 0x... flags 3
+
+    so every ceiling measured so far was on a different pool from the one that
+    fails. One two-rank group brings up 32 channels and RCCL ends up holding
+    roughly a thousand of these per rank, which is the same order as the counts
+    this probe walks, so a ceiling here would be a direct explanation.
+    """
+    hip = _lib()
+    ptrs: list[ctypes.c_void_p] = []
+    reached = 0
+    stopped = f"no ceiling below {limit}"
+    try:
+        while reached < limit:
+            ptr = ctypes.c_void_p()
+            rc = hip.hipExtMallocWithFlags(
+                ctypes.byref(ptr),
+                ctypes.c_size_t(size),
+                ctypes.c_uint(_MALLOC_FLAGS["uncached"]),
+            )
+            if rc != 0:
+                hip.hipGetLastError()
+                stopped = f"malloc stopped first: {_err(rc)}"
+                break
+            ptrs.append(ptr)
+            handle = ctypes.create_string_buffer(_HANDLE_BYTES)
+            rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(handle, ptr)
+            if rc != 0:
+                hip.hipGetLastError()
+                stopped = f"export failed: {_err(rc)}"
+                break
+            reached += 1
+    finally:
+        for ptr in ptrs:
+            hip.hipFree(ptr)
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+    return f"{reached} held, {stopped}"
+

+def _kfd_topology() -> dict:
+    """amd-smi on the CI node reports XGMI as N/A for four of six pairs, which
+    could mean no link or merely no visibility from inside the VM. The driver's
+    own node properties and io_links do not carry that ambiguity."""
+    base = "/sys/class/kfd/kfd/topology/nodes"
+    wanted = (
+        "simd_count",
+        "capability",
+        "gfx_target_version",
+        "location_id",
+        "domain",
+        "drm_render_minor",
+        "num_xcc",
+        "hive_id",
+    )
+    gpus: dict[str, object] = {}
+    cpus: list[str] = []
+    unreadable: list[str] = []
+    try:
+        nodes = sorted(os.listdir(base), key=lambda n: int(n) if n.isdigit() else -1)
+    except OSError as e:
+        return {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}
+    for node in nodes:
+        props: dict[str, str] = {}
+        try:
+            with open(f"{base}/{node}/properties") as f:
+                for line in f:
+                    key, _, value = line.strip().partition(" ")
+                    if key in wanted:
+                        props[key] = value.strip()
+        except OSError as e:
+            # The earlier version dropped these silently, which made an absent
+            # node indistinguishable from one we simply cannot read. In a VM
+            # that difference is the whole question.
+            unreadable.append(f"{node} ({type(e).__name__})")
+            continue
+        if props.get("simd_count", "0") == "0":
+            cpus.append(node)
+            continue
+        links = []
+        try:
+            for link in sorted(os.listdir(f"{base}/{node}/io_links")):
+                fields: dict[str, str] = {}
+                with open(f"{base}/{node}/io_links/{link}/properties") as f:
+                    for line in f:
+                        key, _, value = line.strip().partition(" ")
+                        fields[key] = value.strip()
+                links.append(f"to={fields.get('node_to')} type={fields.get('type')}")
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+        gpus[node] = {"props": props, "io_links": links}
+
+    # RCCL reads this same table, and in CI it claims XGMI towards nodes that
+    # never showed up above. Say so explicitly rather than leaving it to be
+    # noticed by eye.
+    present = set(nodes)
+    for entry in gpus.values():
+        missing = sorted(
+            {
+                link.split("to=", 1)[1].split(" ", 1)[0]
+                for link in entry["io_links"]  # type: ignore[index]
+            }
+            - present
+        )
+        if missing:
+            entry["links_to_absent_nodes"] = missing  # type: ignore[index]
+    return {
+        "nodes_seen": nodes,
+        "cpu_nodes": cpus,
+        "unreadable_nodes": unreadable,
+        "gpus": gpus,
+    }
+

+def _ipc_probe_foreign_device(size: int) -> str:
+    """Allocates on the current device, then exports while a different device is
+    current. This is the mismatch RCCL would hit if it exports a peer buffer
+    without setting the device first."""
+    hip = _lib()
+    count = _hip_device_count()
+    if count < 2:
+        return "skipped: single device"
+    home = _hip_device()
+    ptr = ctypes.c_void_p()
+    rc = hip.hipMalloc(ctypes.byref(ptr), ctypes.c_size_t(size))
+    if rc != 0:
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        return f"malloc failed {_err(rc)}"
+    other = (home + 1) % count
+    try:
+        rc = hip.hipSetDevice(ctypes.c_int(other))
+        if rc != 0:
+            hip.hipGetLastError()
+            return f"setDevice({other}) failed {_err(rc)}"
+        handle = ctypes.create_string_buffer(64)
+        rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(handle, ptr)
+        out = f"home={home} exported_from={other} " + (
+            "ok" if rc == 0 else f"ipc failed {_err(rc)}"
+        )
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+    finally:
+        hip.hipSetDevice(ctypes.c_int(home))
+        hip.hipFree(ptr)
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+    return out
+

+def _ipc_mesh_probe(group, size: int, flags: int) -> str:
+    """Exports one buffer per rank and attaches every peer's. Handles travel
+    over the CPU group, so the device group under test stays untouched.
+
+    The attach side is the one that aborted in CI when
+    HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY was set, and nothing probed it until now.
+    """
+    hip = _lib()
+    ptr = ctypes.c_void_p()
+    rc = hip.hipExtMallocWithFlags(
+        ctypes.byref(ptr), ctypes.c_size_t(size), ctypes.c_uint(flags)
+    )
+    if rc != 0:
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        return f"malloc failed {_err(rc)}"
+
+    handle = _HipIpcMemHandle()
+    rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(ctypes.byref(handle), ptr)
+    hip.hipGetLastError()
+    mine = bytes(handle.reserved) if rc == 0 else None
+    export = "ok" if rc == 0 else f"failed {_err(rc)}"
+
+    peers: list = [None] * group.world_size
+    try:
+        torch.distributed.all_gather_object(peers, mine, group=group.cpu_group)
+    except Exception as e:
+        hip.hipFree(ptr)
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        return f"export {export}, exchange failed {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
+
+    problems = []
+    for peer, raw in enumerate(peers):
+        if peer == group.rank_in_group:
+            continue
+        if raw is None:
+            problems.append(f"rank{peer} exported nothing")
+            continue
+        opened = ctypes.c_void_p()
+        theirs = _HipIpcMemHandle()
+        ctypes.memmove(ctypes.byref(theirs), raw, _HANDLE_BYTES)
+        rc = hip.hipIpcOpenMemHandle(
+            ctypes.byref(opened), theirs, _IPC_LAZY_ENABLE_PEER_ACCESS
+        )
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        if rc != 0:
+            problems.append(f"rank{peer} {_err(rc)}")
+            continue
+        hip.hipIpcCloseMemHandle(opened)
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+
+    hip.hipFree(ptr)
+    hip.hipGetLastError()
+    attach = "ok" if not problems else "; ".join(problems)
+    return f"export {export}, attach {attach}"
+
+
+def _ipc_attach_ceiling(group, size: int, flags: int, limit: int) -> str:
+    """How many of a peer's exports attach before one is refused.
+
+    The export ceiling says nothing about the import side, and the dmabuf
+    implementation breaks there rather than on export, so without this the two
+    implementations cannot be compared at the point where each of them actually
+    fails. One rank exports and the others attach and hold, which means the
+    number the others report can never exceed what that one rank exported, so
+    both counts go into the line.
+    """
+    hip = _lib()
+    source = 0
+    mine = group.rank_in_group == source
+    ptrs: list[ctypes.c_void_p] = []
+    raws: list[bytes] = []
+    opened: list[ctypes.c_void_p] = []
+    stopped = f"no ceiling below {limit}"
+    try:
+        while mine and len(raws) < limit:
+            ptr = ctypes.c_void_p()
+            rc = hip.hipExtMallocWithFlags(
+                ctypes.byref(ptr), ctypes.c_size_t(size), ctypes.c_uint(flags)
+            )
+            if rc != 0:
+                hip.hipGetLastError()
+                stopped = f"malloc stopped first: {_err(rc)}"
+                break
+            ptrs.append(ptr)
+            handle = _HipIpcMemHandle()
+            rc = hip.hipIpcGetMemHandle(ctypes.byref(handle), ptr)
+            hip.hipGetLastError()
+            if rc != 0:
+                stopped = f"export failed: {_err(rc)}"
+                break
+            raws.append(bytes(handle.reserved))
+
+        gathered: list = [None] * group.world_size
+        try:
+            torch.distributed.all_gather_object(
+                gathered, raws if mine else None, group=group.cpu_group
+            )
+        except Exception as e:
+            return f"exchange failed {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
+
+        peer = gathered[source] or []
+        if mine:
+            return f"source, exported {len(raws)}, {stopped}"
+
+        for raw in peer:
+            theirs = _HipIpcMemHandle()
+            ctypes.memmove(ctypes.byref(theirs), raw, _HANDLE_BYTES)
+            got = ctypes.c_void_p()
+            rc = hip.hipIpcOpenMemHandle(
+                ctypes.byref(got), theirs, _IPC_LAZY_ENABLE_PEER_ACCESS
+            )
+            hip.hipGetLastError()
+            if rc != 0:
+                stopped = f"attach failed: {_err(rc)}"
+                break
+            opened.append(got)
+        return f"attached {len(opened)} of {len(peer)}, {stopped}"
+    finally:
+        for got in opened:
+            hip.hipIpcCloseMemHandle(got)
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+        # The exporter has to outlive every attach, so nothing is freed until
+        # all of them have been closed.
+        try:
+            torch.distributed.barrier(group=group.cpu_group)
+        except Exception:
+            logger.warning("[EEP-DEBUG] attach ceiling barrier failed")
+        for ptr in ptrs:
+            hip.hipFree(ptr)
+        hip.hipGetLastError()
+

+    fails, so a pass that only wants to know whether the test itself passes has

+def dump(tag: str, groups: dict | None = None, heavy: bool = False) -> None:
+    """Heavy adds probes that perturb state, so they stay off at the points
+    right before a collective we are trying to observe."""
+    if _off():
+        return
+    try:
+        device = torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+        free, total = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(device)
+        get_settings = getattr(torch._C, "_accelerator_getAllocatorSettings", None)
+        info = {
+            "pid": os.getpid(),
+            "device": device,
+            "hip_device": _hip_device(),
+            "device_fds": _device_fds(),
+            "free_gib": round(free / 2**30, 2),
+            "total_gib": round(total / 2**30, 2),
+            "allocated_gib": round(
+                torch.accelerator.memory_allocated(device) / 2**30, 2
+            ),
+            "reserved_gib": round(torch.accelerator.memory_reserved(device) / 2**30, 2),
+            "allocator_backend": torch.cuda.memory.get_allocator_backend(),
+            "allocator_settings": get_settings() if get_settings else None,
+        }
+        if groups:
+            info["groups"] = {
+                name: {
+                    "rank": g.rank_in_group,
+                    "world_size": g.world_size,
+                    "ranks": list(getattr(g, "ranks", [])),
+                    "device": str(getattr(g, "device", None)),
+                }
+                for name, g in groups.items()
+                if g is not None
+            }
+        info["ipc_probe_6MiB"] = _ipc_probe(6 << 20)
+        info["ipc_probe_plain_6MiB"] = _ipc_probe_plain(6 << 20)
+        # The drop from 1536 in prepare to about 120 at the door happens
+        # somewhere in between, and nothing has measured that stretch yet. A
+        # limit of 256 holds 1.5 GiB for under a tenth of a second, and the same
+        # measurement already runs immediately before a collective that then
+        # succeeds, so it is safe to take here too.
+        info["ipc_export_ceiling_6MiB_256"] = _ipc_export_ceiling(6 << 20, 256)
+        # This one costs what it measures. Two dumps a second apart read 117
+        # and then 0 on the agent, because the 2 MiB exports in the first one
+        # never give their capacity back, so leaving it on turns every later
+        # reading into a reading of this probe. It stays off unless a pass is
+        # specifically asking how much a batch of 2 MiB exports consumes.
+        if _drain_probe():
+            info["ipc_export_ceiling_2MiB_768"] = _ipc_export_ceiling(2 << 20, 768)
+        if heavy:
+            # Burst can exhaust export handles and foreign_device creates a
+            # context on a neighbour card, so neither runs near the collective.
+            info["ipc_probe_burst_64x6MiB"] = _ipc_probe_burst(6 << 20, 64)
+            info["ipc_probe_foreign_device"] = _ipc_probe_foreign_device(6 << 20)
+            # Same size and same limit as the parent's own ceiling below, so
+            # the two lines can be read side by side.
+            info["ipc_probe_fresh_process"] = _ipc_probe_fresh_process(6 << 20, 1536)
+            info["ipc_export_ceiling_2MiB"] = _ipc_export_ceiling(2 << 20, 4096)
+            # 6 MiB is the size RCCL exports most of, and it holds about a
+            # thousand of them per rank, so walk past that.
+            info["ipc_export_ceiling_6MiB"] = _ipc_export_ceiling(6 << 20, 1536)
+        logger.warning("[EEP-DEBUG] %s %s", tag, info)
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.warning("[EEP-DEBUG] %s dump failed: %r", tag, e)

+def warm_each(groups: dict, tag: str) -> None:
+    if _off():
+        return
+    warm_only = _warm_only()
+    stream = torch.Stream(device=next(iter(groups.values())).device)
+    with stream:
+        tensor = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=stream.device)
+        for name, group in groups.items():
+            try:
+                if warm_only:
+                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(tensor, group=group.device_group)
+                    stream.synchronize()
+                    logger.warning("[EEP-DEBUG] %s warm %s ok, warm only", tag, name)
+                    continue

+                # export inside RCCL can land on the wrong one.
+                logger.warning(
+                    "[EEP-DEBUG] %s warm %s ctx hip_device=%s torch_device=%s "
+                    "group_device=%s stream_device=%s",
+                    tag,
+                    name,
+                    _hip_device(),
+                    torch.accelerator.current_device_index(),
+                    getattr(group, "device", None),
+                    stream.device,
+                )
+                # Sizes and flags taken from the two CI failures: 2 MiB with
+                # flags 3 aborted on attach, 6 MiB failed on export.
+                logger.warning(
+                    "[EEP-DEBUG] %s warm %s mesh 2MiB/uncached [%s] 6MiB/default [%s]",

+                    _ipc_mesh_probe(group, 6 << 20, 0x0),
